title: Request: Temporary measurement-epoch grace for p50/p95 during region burst (NovaSystems)
text:
Request: Temporary measurement-epoch grace for p50/p95 during region burst (NovaSystems)

["From: Rachel Torres <rachel.torres@novasystems.com>\\nTo: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 10:31:00 -0700\\nSubject: Impacting spike in US-east; asking for temporary p95 measurement grace\\n\\nHi Irene,\\n\\nQuick note from NovaSystems' ops team — we had a sustained client-side batch that triggered a regional burst on Tuesday night (US-east) and saw a number of p95 breaches in the hosted API dashboard overnight. Our product team reviewed logs and the requests are expected (large batch inference for overnight analytics), but this is artificially inflating the daily p95 measurement window for our contract.\\n\\nCan Redwood provide a temporary measurement-epoch grace or carveout for 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-07 so these events do not count against this month’s p95 commitment while we put runtime batching limits in place? We can send sample logs and a brief evidence package.\\n\\nWhat we need to know:\\n- Whether Redwood can exclude those epochs from the rolling p95 calculation, and how that affects SLA compliance reporting.\\n- Any audit evidence you need (logs, timestamps, request IDs).\\n- Expected timeline for a decision.\\n\\nAttaching a small set of log snippets and a short summary. Thanks — appreciate your help.\\n\\nBest,\\nRachel Torres\\nDirector, Platform Ops\\nNovaSystems\\n\\nAttachments: burst_evidence_snippets.zip (log snippets)\\n", 'From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Rachel Torres <rachel.torres@novasystems.com>\\nCc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 12:08:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Impacting spike in US-east; asking for temporary p95 measurement grace\\n\\nHi Rachel — thanks for the context and the snippets. I’m looping in Karthik (sales) and Marissa (SLO/product) so we can review the ask and confirm next steps.\\n\\nQuick answers up front:\\n- We do offer temporary carveouts in limited cases but need to validate operational evidence and the mitigation plan.\\n- We’ll need the request IDs + a short summary of why the batch occurred (scheduled job, customer mistake, external traffic surge) and confirmation that NovaSystems will apply a runtime fix (eg. batching guard rails).\\n- Tentative timeline: we can do a rapid assessment and respond with one of: approved carveout, approved with rollforward conditions, or deny (with rationale) within 72 hours after receiving full evidence.\\n\\nMarissa — can you review the attached snippets and advise what evidence set we need to classify this as a transient event eligible for a measurement-epoch grace? Also, if we approve, what metrics/reporting change would we show in the customer-facing SLA report?\\n\\nIrene\\nIrene Choi\\nHead of Customer Reliability\\nRedwood Inference\\n', 'From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Rachel Torres <rachel.torres@novasystems.com>\\nCc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 13:05:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Impacting spike in US-east; asking for temporary p95 measurement grace\\n\\nRachel — appreciate the rapid flag. Two commercial points while the technical review happens:\\n1) If we approve a carveout, we typically record an \\"epoch grace\\" event in the monthly SLA report and include a short justification so it\'s auditable. That does not change billing, but it does affect whether we consider the month in breach for contractual purposes.\\n2) For multi-month/recurring burst patterns we require a committed remediation plan (timelines + owners) and will convert the carveout to a conditional rollforward if the remediation misses milestones.\\n\\nCan you confirm whether NovaSystems wants this treated as a one-off transient carveout or as a temporary conditional rollforward tied to the mitigation plan? Also happy to schedule a 30-min call to align on remediation timelines with your SREs.\\n\\nThanks — Karthik\\nKarthik Iyer\\nEnterprise Account Executive\\nRedwood Inference\\n', 'From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Irene Choi <irene_ichoi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Torres <rachel.torres@novasystems.com>\\nDate: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Impacting spike in US-east; asking for temporary p95 measurement grace\\n\\nHi all — I reviewed the log snippets (thanks Rachel) and ran them past SRE. Summary of findings and proposal:\\n\\nObservations:\\n- The traffic was concentrated between 02:10–04:30 UTC on 2026-10-06 and matches a scheduled batch spike (large payloads + long generation sequences).\\n- The requests in the snippets show repeated heavy KV-cache misses and full attention runs that produced long tail latencies; these are consistent with batch-induced cold-cache behavior.\\n- There is no indication of a broader regional capacity failure (hosts remained healthy; no OOMs, retries are customer-driven).\\n\\nEligibility criteria check (for a measurement-epoch grace):\\n- Transient: yes (single window, predictable pattern).\\n- Customer mitigation plan: pending (NovaSystems indicated they will add batching limits).\\n- Auditability: partial — we have request IDs and timestamps; we asked for the job config to confirm it’s a scheduled nightly job.\\n\\nProposal (technical):\\n- Approve a 72-hour measurement-epoch grace for 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-07 conditional on NovaSystems providing the job config and confirming the change to batching limits within 5 business days.\\n- We will apply a labeled carveout in the monthly SLA report and include the attached \\"transient-window-smoothing-proposal.pdf\\" that documents the decision rationale.\\n- If NovaSystems fails to submit remediation evidence in 5 business days, the grace will be converted to a conditional rollforward with milestones and potential credit clawback language (per contract).\\n\\nAttached: transient-window-smoothing-proposal.pdf (policy template), SLO-exception-checklist.xlsx (evidence checklist).\\n\\nRachel — if that approach sounds acceptable, please reply with the job config (or a short note confirming it was a scheduled job) and attach the remediation timeline. We can then finalize approval and produce the updated SLA report entry.\\n\\nRegards,\\nMarissa Cole\\nProduct Manager, SLOs & Observability\\nRedwood Inference\\n', 'From: Rachel Torres <rachel.torres@novasystems.com>\\nTo: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_ichoi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Impacting spike in US-east; asking for temporary p95 measurement grace\\n\\nMarissa / Irene / Karthik — thanks, that plan is fine. Confirming:\\n- NovaSystems will share the job config and a short remediation timeline by end of day Monday (2026-10-18).\\n- We accept the conditional 72-hour measurement-epoch grace for 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-07 under the terms you described.\\n\\nI’ve attached the evidence bundle (burst_evidence_snippets.zip) and included our remediation owner contact: Sam Patel (sam.patel@novasystems.com). We’ll also accept the proposed SLA report notation.\\n\\nLet us know when Redwood publishes the updated report entry. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.\\n\\nBest,\\nRachel\\nDirector, Platform Ops\\nNovaSystems\\n\\nAttachments: burst_evidence_snippets.zip\\n']
